label: a
rationale: Run arithmetic first: this run has 32 batches, and 32 > 10x3, so the generic ten-group bound cannot cover it; the engine's current facts report max_groups 12 and alpha-groups.mjs enforces full coverage, so this partition uses 12 groups. Hopf-hecke wholeness: batches 1 and 3 are the run's only hopf-hecke-algebras batches, so one Alpha must own both; their 15+9 = 24 items make this the lightest group. Twelve groups is also the load optimum: 302 items over 12 groups forces some group to hold at least 26, while eleven groups cannot keep the maximum below 29 (batch 29's 18 items plus the two smallest partners 5+6 already total 29 inside one triple, and if the single 2-batch group is not the hopf pair then the 24-item hopf triple needs any partner >= 5, again reaching 29). This partition attains maximum 26 with minimum 24, spread 2, the best achievable. Coherence: the pair keeps the 3->1 edge (3) internal; 3->2 (5) must cross because adding batch 2 would make the group 35 > 26.

label: b
rationale: Coxeter foundations cluster, 11+8+7 = 26 items (the allowed maximum): exchange and reduced-word theorems (batch 2), canonical roots and faithful reflections (7), Tits cones, chambers and parabolic stabilizers (9). Internal dependency weight 10 (7->2 4, 9->7 4, 9->2 2); the roots and Tits-cone pages consume batch 2's presentation and exchange machinery. Load/coherence tradeoff: batch 2 is this group's heaviest member and an almost universal supplier, but 11+8+7 already sits at the 26 cap, so no 8-item or larger foundation batch can share the group without breaching the window.

label: c
rationale: Finite reflection theory, 9+6+11 = 26 items: real forms and reflection geometry (4), finite reflection arrangements and spherical Coxeter complexes (17), finite invariants and coinvariant gradings (20). Internal weight 12 (17->4 6, 20->4 5, 20->17 1). Batch 4 is the reflection-theory supplier hub (7->4 6, 13->4 6, 19->4 6, 9->4 5, 27->4 5, 29->4 5 also enter it) and only two partners fit the 24-26 window; 27->4 and 29->4 are impossible here because 13+9 = 22 is below the floor and 18+9 = 27 above the cap, so those crossings are forced by the load window rather than by the grouping.

label: d
rationale: Davis-complex cluster, 7+12+7 = 26 items: spherical parabolic cosets and the Davis complex (26), Davis CAT(0) geometry and finite-subgroup fixed points (30), finite lattice projections and Coxeter chain labels (5). Internal weight 7 (30->26). Load/coherence tradeoff: the 26+30 pair is 19 items and needs one 5-7 item partner to reach the floor; batch 5 (7 items) fills it to exactly 26, while the other partners of that size were needed to hold heavier internal edges elsewhere (17 with the 12-weight reflection triple in group c, 16 with the 16->12 edge in group f).

label: e
rationale: Metric geometry of Coxeter complexes, 8+7+10 = 25 items: polyhedral gluings and intrinsic metrics (6), spherical simplex metrics, angular links and cones (8), large spherical metric flags and the Moussong girth theorem (22). Internal weight 10 (8->6 5, 22->8 4, 22->6 1). This keeps the run's strongest metric-geometry edges in one Alpha; 22->11 (4) and 30->6/8/22 (4 each) cross because batches 11 and 30 anchor their own load-balanced groups (g and d).

label: f
rationale: Bruhat-order combinatorics, 8+10+7 = 25 items: parabolic subgroups and double-coset geometry (10), Bruhat subword order and lifting (12), Bruhat interval labels, shellings and Mobius functions (16). Internal weight 9 (16->12 6, 12->10 2, 16->10 1). Capturing the 16->12 edge (6) anchors this triple; 16->2 (3) and 16->5 (2) stay crossing because batches 2 and 5 are pinned to the foundations and Davis-complex groups that need them for heavier internal edges.

label: g
rationale: CAT(0) local-to-global pair, 12+13 = 25 items: comparison/link criteria and local-globalization (11) beside short-loop polygons and quantitative energy decrease (15). Internal weight 4 (15->11). Both are the metric-geometry medium batches; pairing them keeps the energy-decrease machinery next to the local-global criterion it feeds, and the 12+13 = 25 total already clears the 24-item floor without a third batch.

label: h
rationale: Finite and classical Coxeter theory, 10+7+9 = 26 items: complete classification of finite diagrams (13), crystallographic root lattices and Weyl-group interfaces (21), descents, Poincare polynomials and growth (25). Internal weight 7 (21->13 4, 25->13 3). The 27->13 edge (5) cannot be internal: 13+27 = 23 items is below the 24 floor and any third batch breaks the 26 cap; 20->13, 19->13 and 31->13 (4 each) cross because those suppliers anchor heavier triples.

label: i
rationale: Hecke/sortable interface pair, 8+18 = 26 items: Coxeter-Artin and Hecke interfaces (14) beside Coxeter Euler forms and sortable chamber cones (29). No internal dependency edge. Indivisible-load limit reported explicitly: batch 29's 18 items cannot be balanced by Step 2; its only legal partners are 6-, 7- and 8-item batches (18+6 = 24, 18+7 = 25, 18+8 = 26), 18 plus any two other batches exceeds 26, and the 10-weight 32->29 edge is impossible to internalize because 18+5 = 23 is below the floor and any third batch overshoots the cap; the equal-value alternative (29,7) would disturb the 10-weight roots triple in group b.

label: j
rationale: Noncrossing and bipartite cluster, 7+9+9 = 25 items: finite reflection length and moved spaces (18), bipartite Coxeter elements and ordered root complexes (19), noncrossing partition lattices and Kreweras complements (31). Internal weight 12 (31->19 6, 19->18 3, 31->18 3), the run's densest capturable triple. Edges 31->13 and 19->13 (4 each) cross to the classification group h because batch 13 must stay with the finite-classification material.

label: k
rationale: Weak-order and sortable combinatorics, 9+10+5 = 24 items: inversions and lattice operations (23), heaps, commutation classes and fully commutative elements (28), sortable projections and finite Cambrian lattices (32). Internal weight 7 (32->23 4, 28->23 3). Batch 32 is the run's lightest batch (5 items) and anchors this floor-weight group; its 10-weight 32->29 edge is unavoidably crossing because 5+18 = 23 items cannot form a floor-legal pair and any third batch breaks the 26 cap.

label: l
rationale: Affine Coxeter pair, 11+13 = 24 items: affine reflections, coroot translations and alcoves (24) with affine diagrams and the semidefinite classification (27). Internal weight 6 (27->24). The 11+13 = 24 sum sits exactly on the load floor, and this pair is the only way to keep the 27->24 edge internal: a third batch in either group would push the total past 26, so the affine reading block stays a two-batch group.
